text: Isaiah Moliga-Puletasi (he/him) is a third-year at Pomona College majoring in English and art history with a minor in data science. His data science research seeks to archive and record literature, material, and cultural artifacts.

title: Agricultural Production Statistics in New Zealand: Total number of sheep in New Zealand (1935-2024)
text:
Citation: This dataset comes from TidyTuesday’s 2-17-26 weekly data challenge, Agricultural Production Statistics in New Zealand, curated by Jen Richmond. The data is dervied from Figure.NZ.
Description: The Agricultural Production Statistics in New Zealand dataset provides quantitative information on New Zealand’s agricultural systems. By collecting agricultural data in New Zealand, we can see the human-agriculture relations that arise over time. This dataset is particulary interested in the decline of sheep populations relative to humans over.

library(tidyverse)

dataset <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-02-17/dataset.csv')

new_dataset <- dataset |>
    dplyr::filter(measure == "Total Sheep") |>
    dplyr::select(year_ended_june, measure, value)

new_dataset |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = year_ended_june, y = value)) +
    geom_line() + 
    labs(
        title = "Total number of sheep in New Zealand (1935-2024)",
        x = "Year",
        y = ""
    )

title: MTA Permanent Art Catalog: Number of art pieces across NY transit (2025)
text:
Citation: This dataset comes from TidyTuesday’s 7-22-25 weekly data challenge, MTA Permanent Art Collection, curated by Jon Harmon and suggested by Georgios Karamanis. The data is dervied from State of New York’s public data on MTA’s art catalog.
Description: The MTA Permanent Art Collection dataset collects artist, art, and geographic data across NY transit systems to examine its collection of public art. By documenting public art information, NY can examine its relationship to arts and culture, as well as transit infrastructure development.

library(tidyverse)

mta_art <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2025/2025-07-22/mta_art.csv')
station_lines <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2025/2025-07-22/station_lines.csv')

new_mta_art <- mta_art |> 
    select(agency, artist) |>
    group_by(agency) 

new_mta_art |> 
    ggplot(aes(x= agency)) +
    geom_bar() + 
    labs(
        x = "Transit agency",
        y = "",
        title = "Number of art pieces across NY transit (2025)"
    )
